C++.justification: `int32_t small = static_cast<int32_t>(big);` explicit narrowing conversion (rung ii); C++20 `std::in_range<int32_t>(big)` also available for a checked-style guard.

Go.justification: small := int32(big) -- Go's ordinary explicit narrowing conversion (rung ii; no checked-conversion stdlib op exists).

Java.justification: int small; try { small = Math.toIntExact(big); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { small = 0; } — Math.toIntExact is the standard checked narrowing operation.

Kotlin.justification: val small = big.toInt() — explicit ordinary narrowing conversion (rung ii); Kotlin stdlib has no checked Long-to-Int conversion returning an optional, so the plain explicit conversion (bit-truncating) is used.

Python.fragment:
import ctypes
small = ctypes.c_int32(big).value
return small
Python.justification: ctypes.c_int32 is a standard-library signed 32-bit representation and its explicit construction is a standard narrowing conversion. The unchanged preference ladder therefore reaches rung (ii) without a named-substitution exception.

Quidra.citation: numeric-and-bin.md 'Conversion': `int32(big)` is the ordinary explicit narrowing cast; 'Integer narrowing never wraps or clamps' and is deterministically range-checked at runtime (rung ii, frozen checked-mode behavior).

Swift.fragment:
let small = Int32(exactly: big) ?? 0
return small
Swift.justification: let small = Int32(exactly: big) ?? 0 — rung (i) failable initializer reports out-of-range as nil.

TypeScript.justification: const small = Number(big) | 0; — explicit narrowing to 32-bit representation via documented ToInt32 bitwise conversion (rung ii); no checked/optional narrowing op exists in stdlib.

Zig.fragment: const small: i32 = std.math.cast(i32, big) orelse 0;
Zig.justification: std.math.cast(i32, big) returns ?i32 (rung i, checked conversion yielding optional) — explicit, documented.
